title: Sonnet model returns 'Rate limit reached' despite 0% usage
body:
## Bug Description

Sonnet model (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) immediately returns `Rate limit reached` error when spawning a subagent via Claude Code Agent tool, despite usage dashboard showing 0% Sonnet usage.

This issue has been persistent since the morning of 2026-03-18 (over 24 hours).

## Environment
- Claude Code running inside VS Code extension (Dev Container)
- Platform: Linux (WSL2)
- Opus 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 work normally in the same session

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Claude Code in VS Code
2. Spawn a subagent with `model: "sonnet"`
3. Agent immediately fails (221ms) with `Rate limit reached`
4. Check usage dashboard — shows 0% Sonnet usage, 4% All models

## Expected Behavior
Sonnet subagent should execute normally when usage is at 0%.

## Actual Behavior
- Instant rejection (221ms response time — no actual API call attempted)
- Error: `API Error: Rate limit reached`
- Haiku and Opus agents work fine in the same session

## Dashboard at time of report
- Current session: 6% used
- Weekly — All models: 4% used
- Weekly — Sonnet only: 0% used
author: xlurie

top_comments.author: willfindlay
top_comments.body:
Confirming the same behavior on my end.

- Platform: Linux (WSL2), Claude Code CLI (not VS Code extension)
- Parent model: Opus 4.6 (1M context)
- Sonnet subagents fail instantly (~200ms) with `Rate limit reached`
- Opus and Haiku subagents work fine in the same session
- Omitting the `model` parameter (inheriting the parent Opus model) also works fine
- Issue has persisted throughout the evening of 2026-03-20

top_comments.author: xlurie
top_comments.body:
**Found a workaround for one possible cause of this.**

In my case, I had custom env vars in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` that explicitly set the model IDs with the `[1m]` suffix:

```json
"ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "claude-opus-4-6[1m]",
"ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "claude-sonnet-4-6[1m]"
```

Claude Code internally appends `[1m]` when running with 1M context, so this resulted in the model ID becoming `claude-sonnet-4-6[1m][1m]` — an invalid ID that the API rejects instantly as

top_comments.author: willfindlay
top_comments.body:
> Note: this may not explain every case (e.g. @willfindlay's setup may not use these env vars), but if you've set model overrides anywhere in your environment, check for this duplication.

Actually that was the issue in my setup too. Thanks a bunch for the workaround. This is still probably a bug though. Claude Code should not append the [1m] prefix when it's already there.
